Майтаке.about: Maitake has been studied in animals: both meta-analyses of the polysaccharide were performed on mouse models; there is not a single RCT on humans in the pool.
Майтаке.caution: The authors of both meta-analyses noted the low quality of the included studies and the risk of bias in selection, detection, and reporting.
Майтаке.course: not specified in abstracts for humans
Майтаке.food_sources: Sources are not discussed in abstracts: both meta-analyses study isolated fungal polysaccharides, not food products.
Майтаке.guidelines: There are no recommendations for maitake in the pool: two sources are meta-analyses on animal models with SYRCLE risk of bias assessment.
Майтаке.how_to_choose: There is nothing to evaluate: there is no human dose data in the pool, so any extracts and combinations remain outside the scope of study.
mechs: Maitake polysaccharide suppressed tumor growth and increased remission rates in animal experiments
In animal models, an increase in CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes, NK cells and macrophages was noted
Changes in immune parameters in animals
Transfer of data from animal models to humans in the pool is not justified
The effect in humans has not been studied
Майтаке.myths: “Meta-analysis proves benefit” - these are meta-analyses on animals; according to the rules of the project, they are not transferred to humans. “Immunity confirmed” - the authors themselves write that the quality of the work is low.
Майтаке.name: Maitake
Майтаке.onset: Not studied in humans: the timing of effect in both meta-analyses was based on animal models.
Майтаке.title: Maitake
Майтаке.who_needs: For no one, according to the pool: All 44 papers in the two meta-analyses were performed on animal models, not humans.
